column1: #vocabulary_authority: Dfam / RepeatMasker class notation, arranged on the Wicker et al. (2007) hierarchy
#vocabulary_status: PROVISIONAL -- superseded when the unified Dfam/Repbase classification is released
# Maps a raw class/family label as emitted by a tool onto a canonical
# hierarchical path. This file is INPUT, not logic: the pipeline reads it at
# `harmonize` time and never hardcodes a class name. Re-mapping is a re-run of
# harmonize + summarize; the per-base segmentation is class-agnostic and is not
# Raw labels are ALWAYS preserved verbatim alongside the canonical path in every
# output, so no information is lost to a mapping decision and any mapping can be
# audited or reversed after the fact.
#   Truncate at the deepest level actually supported by the label. A label that
#   only says "DNA" maps to repeat:TE:ClassII and stops -- it does not guess an order.
#   raw_label      Label as it appears in the tool's output, matched case-insensitively.
#                  A trailing `*` makes it a prefix rule (longest match wins), which
#                  absorbs the endless RepeatMasker subfamily suffixes.
#   tool_id        Tool this rule applies to, or `*` for all tools.
#   canonical_v2   Reserved for the unified Dfam/Repbase classification. Left blank
#                  until it lands; when populated, both vocabularies can be carried
#                  simultaneously so tracks can be rebuilt under either.
#   is_te          yes|no|unknown -- answers design question 1.3 directly.
#   confidence     high|medium|low -- how certain the mapping is. `low` entries are
#                  the ones most worth your review.
#   note           Rationale, and any place the tool's usage diverges from Dfam's.

column1: # Emitted with a Class/ prefix (e.g. "DNA/DTA", "MITE/DTT", "LTR/RLC"); rules
# match the bare code and the ingest step strips any leading "Class/" prefix
# All six LTR codes below (RL*) are tool_id `*`. RLG/RLC/RLR were observed in
# ltrdenovo (NGSEP) output emitted exactly as EDTA emits them; the remaining
# three are widened with them because RL* is one closed, published series in
# Wicker et al. 2007 -- splitting it by tool would mean an unobserved sibling
# code silently degrades to bare "repeat" the first time any tool emits it,
# which is the failure mode this block exists to prevent.
# The non-LTR codes further down stay edta-scoped. That asymmetry is deliberate
# and narrower than it looks: those series (DT*, RI*, RS*) are larger and their
# per-code semantics vary more between tools, so widening them would assert
# agreement across vocabularies we have not checked against real output.
